summary: Unreclaimed tokens on early websocket disconnect causing gradual 429 accumulation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a slow accumulation of 429 throttles over multiple hours tied to long-lived websocket streaming clients. Impact: Several of Aurora Analytics' worker fleets began receiving sporadic 429s despite aggregate tenant usage remaining under quota. Observed behavior: 429s correlate with clients that open a websocket and disconnect within ~300ms of opening (pre-auth handshake or network blip). Expected behavior: Tokens reserved for a connection should be returned when session terminates before significant token consumption, or token reservation should not occur until after handshake completion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision tenant on dedicated pool (Aurora Analytics test org) with typical burst quota settings.
2) Create a client that establishes websocket sessions in quick open-close cycles (<500ms) at ~20 connections/sec.
3) Observe tenant token utilization and the X-RateLimit-* headers on subsequent valid sessions.
4) After ~2-3 hours, trigger normal sustained streaming and observe intermittent 429s despite dashboard showing spare burst credits.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Reservation occurs at connection accept time, not post-handshake; fast client aborts skip release path.
Hypothesis 2: Health checks or upstream proxies are reusing connection IDs leading to stale reservation records.
Finding: Instrumented traces show reservation entries tied to conn IDs that never emit 'release' events when a TCP RST occurs before upgrade completion.
Reproduction: Customer stress test (short-lived ws opens at 20/s) reproduces token drift in ~90 minutes on dedicated pool with default burst settings.
Scope: Impact limited to websocket sessions that are terminated before handshake completion. Non-websocket HTTP streaming paths not affected.
Risk: Left unfixed, customers with aggressive short-lived session patterns will exhaust burst credits over time and receive 429s during normal traffic.
Related checks: rate-limiter TTL does not expire quickly enough to recover reservations when client disconnects during handshake.
resolution: Workaround: Advise customer to throttle short-lived connection rate (client-side backoff) and temporarily increase per-route burst capacity. Implemented temporary console flag for the customer's org to extend token refill smoothing window. Permanent fix: landed a code change to defer reserving tokens until handshake success and added a cleanup path on early TCP/TLS teardown. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1872. Rollout plan: canary to 5% of dedicated pools on 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-15 after telemetry verification. Post-deploy monitoring: add synthetic short-lived connection test and alert if tenant_burst_drift > 5% over 2 hours.
